answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 for 30 days before receiving a fixed daily order quota. Whether it sells saffron or onyx, each agent occupies a vertex in the trading graph and must fund its own deposit. Creating 1,000 identities therefore ties up $100,000 for a month; splitting one wallet creates no extra quota without extra capital. This makes a sybil swarm costly through locked funds and forgone returns.
